trial_name.text: ISIS 301012-CS5 (also referred to as ISIS-CS5), the single phase 3 trial in patients with HoFH

citations.quote: The efficacy of mipomersen in patients with HoFH was examined in one phase 3 clinical trial, ISIS-CS5.
In Trial ISIS 301012-CS5 (individuals with HoFH), the mean percent change in LDL-C was -24.7% for individuals in the mipomersen group and -3.3% for individuals in the placebo group (p<0.001).

key_safety.text: Most common AEs were injection-site reactions (84% mipomersen vs 33% placebo) and flu-like symptoms (30% vs 16%). Hepatotoxicity: in the HoFH trial 12% (4/34) of mipomersen patients had ALT ≥3xULN vs 0% placebo; median increase in hepatic fat fraction 9.6% vs 0.02% placebo. Mipomersen is highly immunogenic (ADA 33% at Week 50).

citations.quote: Injection-site reactions were the most commonly-reported adverse events in the mipomersen development program: 84% of mipomersen-treated patients compared with 33% of placebo-treated patients.
In the phase 3 clinical trials, flu-like symptoms were reported by 30% of patients treated with mipomersen and by 16% of patients treated with placebo.

KYNAMRO can cause elevations in transaminases. In the KYNAMRO clinical trial in patients with HoFH, 4 (12%) of the 34 patients treated with KYNAMRO compared with 0% of the 17 patients treated with placebo had at least one elevation in alanine aminotransferase (ALT) \ge 3\times upper limit of normal (ULN).
The median increase in hepatic fat fraction was 9.6% in the mipomersen group versus 0.02% in the placebo group (below table from Dr. Craig's review).
the percentage of subjects treated with mipomersen who developed anti-drug antibody (ADA) increased from 4% at Week 13 to 20% at Week 28 to 33% at Week 50.

detail.text: WARNING: RISK OF HEPATOTOXICITY — KYNAMRO can cause elevations in transaminases; 4 (12%) of 34 mipomersen patients vs 0% of 17 placebo had ALT ≥3xULN, and it increases hepatic fat (median absolute increase 10% after 26 weeks in HeFH/hyperlipidemia trials), a risk factor for advanced liver disease including steatohepatitis and cirrhosis.

citations.quote: ## WARNING: RISK OF HEPATOTOXICITY

KYNAMRO can cause elevations in transaminases. In the KYNAMRO clinical trial in patients with HoFH, 4 (12%) of the 34 patients treated with KYNAMRO compared with 0% of the 17 patients treated with placebo had at least one elevation in alanine aminotransferase (ALT) \ge 3\times upper limit of normal (ULN).

KYNAMRO also increases hepatic fat, with or without concomitant increases in transaminases. In the trials in patients with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) and hyperlipidemia, the median absolute increase in hepatic fat was 10% after 26 weeks of treatment, from 0% at baseline, measured by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Hepatic steatosis is a risk factor for advanced liver disease; including steatohepatitis and cirrhosis [see *Warnings and Precautions* (5.1)].

detail.text: Because of the risk of hepatotoxicity, KYNAMRO is available only through a restricted program under a REMS called the KYNAMRO REMS, with elements to assure safe use to mitigate the risk of elevated liver transaminases and hepatic steatosis.

citations.quote: Because of the risk of hepatotoxicity, KYNAMRO is available only through a restricted program under a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) called the KYNAMRO REMS [see *Warnings and Precautions* (5.2)].

we have also determined that Kynamro (mipomersen sodium) can be approved only if elements necessary to assure safe use are required as part of a REMS to mitigate the risk of elevated liver transaminases and hepatic steatosis

vote.text: The advisory committee met on 18 October 2012; when asked if the efficacy and safety data supported marketing for treatment of HoFH, the committee voted 9 "yes" and 6 "no".

citations.quote: The Division's advisory committee met on 18 October 2012 to discuss the efficacy and safety of mipomersen when used as a therapeutic option for patients with HoFH. When asked if the efficacy and safety data for mipomersen supported marketing for the treatment of HoFH, the committee voted 9 "yes" and 6 "no".

orphan_indication.text: Treatment of homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH) is an orphan indication.

citations.quote: This memo summarizes the basis of the regulatory action for this new drug application seeking an orphan indication of the treatment of homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH).
Because the treatment of HoFH is an orphan indication, the company was not required to address the study of mipomersen in the pediatric population.

summary.text: Kynamro (mipomersen), a first-in-class antisense oligonucleotide, was reviewed as a standard (Type 1 NME 505(b)(1)) application for the orphan indication of HoFH and approved January 29, 2013 following a 9-to-6 advisory committee vote, with a REMS and four postmarketing requirements.
